title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
description:
arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes. Existing workflows fragment evidence across versions, evaluation cases, and execution traces. We present SkillLens, an interactive human-LLM system for diagnosing and refining agent skills. description:

title: Evaluating the Participation of Proactive Scouting Agents in Real-time Human Team Meetings
description:
arXiv:2611.28009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An open research question is whether the addition of conversational AI agents to real-time discussions among human teams enhances group performance. This study tested the value of adding proactive scouting agents to teams engaged in collaborative forecasting tasks. title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
description:
arXiv:2611.28012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates.
